title: Expire ordinary Attempt evidence and expose the latest cleanup result

gates.name: Python typecheck
gates.command: docker compose run --rm --no-deps backend python -m mypy src/face_moment

gates.name: Diagnostic retention command and API tests
gates.command: docker compose run --rm backend python -m pytest tests/diagnostics/test_retention_cleanup.py tests/diagnostics/test_retention_api.py

evidence_required: FT-007-AC-004 RED: ordinary core Attempts/evidence never expire, no promoted-subset preservation path or idempotent owner-ordered command exists, and authorized staff cannot observe a latest cleanup result; GREEN: the next linear migration, diagnostics expiry boundary and promo command apply strict controlled 90-day cutoffs, make owner data inaccessible before idempotent artifact deletion, confirm and delete an old core Attempt even when no diagnostic_evidence row exists, preserve only the curated promoted subset, reject an overlapping invocation without replacing the active latest result, record success/failure/interruption and confirmed counts in one latest-result row, safely rerun, and expose the exact no-store operator/developer page/API while denying photographer/unauthenticated access; decisive comparison: disposable ordinary/no-evidence/incomplete/promoted fixtures and private object prefix before/after success, injected failure, orphaned-running recovery, concurrent invocation, rerun and each staff role; artifact: migration/command/API/security evidence under .tasks/TASK-086-T3-FT-007-W3/.
purpose: Implement destructive ordinary retention through the accepted owner order and make its latest applied cutoffs, counts and failure state observable without an internal scheduler or history subsystem.
success_outcome: Ordinary Attempts/evidence older than the fixed cutoff become inaccessible and owner-cleaned, curated promoted data survives, failure/interruption stays truthful, rerun converges safely and authorized staff see exactly one sanitized latest result.
anti_goals: Do not implement FT-009 log storage/search, FT-010 annotation behavior, FT-011 promotion UI/Calibration or FT-012 Photo purge.
Do not add cleanup history, a jobs table, internal scheduler, reliable queue, backup/restore or cross-owner cascade.
Do not mutate production credentials, run against operator/default data or expose raw object identities, participant data or tracebacks.

forbidden_scope: Production PostgreSQL/MinIO, operator/default Attempts/evidence and production timer configuration
Photo, processing, serving-control, staff-access or diagnostics rows outside their named owner commands
FT-009 technical-log implementation and FT-010/FT-011 product behavior
stop_conditions: Cleanup cannot make owner data inaccessible and converge without a cross-owner write/cascade or generic jobs subsystem.
Promoted subset preservation cannot be proven without retaining the whole ordinary bundle, Promo screenshot or technical logs.
A failed/interrupted run cannot remain observable and safely rerunnable through one latest-result row.
Destructive/auth probes cannot be limited to disposable rows/objects with known state, safe rerun and complete cleanup.

constraints: Primary orchestration/latest-result owner is promo; diagnostics first expires only its own data and returns eligible Attempt IDs/counts, then promo deletes only its own confirmed rows.
Use fixed UTC 90-day ordinary cutoffs and expose the fixed technical-log cutoff without claiming FT-009 deletion implementation; no mutable operator cutoff or request-triggered cleanup is added.

Promo selects expired core Attempt UUIDs and diagnostics confirms each after owner-local convergence; a missing diagnostic_evidence row is an explicit no-op confirmation, never an exclusion from cleanup.

The command holds one project-scoped non-blocking PostgreSQL advisory lock, exits 2 without mutation when another run is active, and after lock acquisition marks an orphaned running result interrupted before a fresh run; production timer activation remains TASK-087 scope.

Use unique disposable Attempts/evidence/promoted subsets and private object prefix with controlled time, known initial state, injected failures, safe rerun, decisive owner reads and complete task-owned cleanup.
Resolve the actual direct Alembic predecessor and prove only this revision's round trip/data preservation; never downgrade a shared operator/default database.
invariants: Each owner deletes only its own rows/objects and no database cascade crosses capability ownership.
Ordinary cleanup never deletes the curated promoted subset or restores already expired content on rerun.
Failure/interruption never fabricates success counts; overlap never replaces the active run identity or counts; one latest result remains observable and sanitized.
Staff reads do not start cleanup and reveal no raw object identity, participant payload, credential or traceback.
verification_targets: Disposable controlled-time command fixtures prove strict cutoff inclusion/exclusion, diagnostics-before-promo order, ordinary/no-evidence/incomplete expiry, promoted preservation, idempotent missing-object handling, orphaned-running interruption, overlapping exit 2 with unchanged active result, injected owner failure and successful safe rerun with one latest-result row.
Migration and owner tracing prove one Base/Alembic stream, no cross-owner cascade/direct write, no cleanup history/jobs/internal scheduler and no mutation of Photo/processing/serving state.

Staff API/page fixtures prove never-run and available shapes, exact cutoffs/counts/outcome/error, operator/developer access, photographer/unauthenticated denial, no-store and sanitized evidence using only disposable principals/state.
